why: Choosing jars with no two neighbours is House Robber: at each jar you either skip it (keep the best so far) or take it plus the best answer ending two jars back.
hints: Look at the last jar. Either Andrew takes it or he doesn't. What does each choice say about the jar before it?
Let best[i] be the most chocolates using jars 0..i. Then best[i] = max(best[i-1], best[i-2] + jars[i]).
Only the last two values are needed, so roll two variables through the array: O(n) time, O(1) space.
pitfalls: Taking every other jar starting at index 0 or 1 is not always optimal; in the example the best picks are jars 1, 3 and 6 (gaps of 2 and 3).
A single jar: the answer is its count.
Empty jars (0) are fine; never pick a negative baseline.
